title: Sabotage and terrorism: risk questions, not promises
excerpt: Separate facts, property damage and insurance questions for companies in Moldova without alarming scenarios or promised specialist cover.

seo.description: Distinguish factual findings, legal classification, property and interruption questions. Informational preparation without confirmed specialist insurance.
seo.keywords: sabotage terrorism insurance, incident records, business continuity Moldova, property damage, insurance definitions

content:
Sabotage, terrorism, vandalism and other intentional acts should not be treated as interchangeable insurance terms. For a company in the Republic of Moldova, administrative assessment starts with relevant property, services and documents, not alarming scenarios. Legal classification of an event and its treatment under a contract are different questions. Each needs the appropriate professional competence and supporting information.

This is an informational article. It confirms no special policy through ING Broker, describes no attack methods and provides no installation-security instructions. Where there is actual danger, safety and competent authorities' instructions take priority. Sensitive information must not be published or sent through open forms. Preparing an insurance file is not a reason to investigate unsafe circumstances independently.

Do not begin with an incident label

A news report or internal suspicion may use a term before facts are established. In company records, separate observations, sources and dates. Do not present an assumption as an official finding. If an authority or specialist has reached conclusions, identify the relevant document and the limits of what it establishes. A short management summary should retain that distinction.

Seek competent advice for legal assessment. For insurance, ask how the actual contract defines the relevant terms. News categories do not determine protection. A word's informal use may differ from its legal or contractual meaning. This article does not establish equivalence between those uses or determine how an individual event should be classified for a particular policy.

What a company can prepare administratively

Describe activities, property categories and service dependencies generally. Inventories and ownership or use documents help identify what is being considered. Do not publish sensitive locations, access plans, guarding procedures or vulnerabilities. Any need for detailed information should be established separately through controlled channels, with a clear purpose and appropriate recipients rather than a public request for opinions.

A summary can distinguish owner, tenant, operator and service provider for another entity. These roles are not automatically equivalent. Contractual obligations and responsibilities require examination of documents. The working sheet organizes facts without unnecessary exposure; it does not certify a security standard. An address alone cannot identify every owner or responsibility for assets present there.

Separate material damage from business interruption

Physical damage and a service stoppage can have different consequences. Record the affected asset, expenses and operational impact without deciding cause before findings. Do not combine estimates, invoices and deferred revenue into one amount labelled a sabotage loss. Their documentary status and purpose differ, even where the company is discussing the same period of interrupted activity.

Ask which connection between an event and financial loss the proposed wording requires. Property insurance does not automatically establish interruption protection. A liability clause does not automatically describe the company's own damage. Distinguishing these questions does not confirm availability of a particular product or extension. It helps identify what still needs an explicit answer for the actual company.

Intentional conduct does not mean one universal exclusion

Do not simplify documents by claiming that intentional always means included or excluded in the same way. The people addressed, definitions and precise wording matter to specialist assessment. This article neither interprets those provisions nor assigns intent to a person. Ask for an explicit explanation of the relevant terms rather than extending an informal generalization to every situation.

Use the same factual description when comparing proposed documents. Where terms differ, retain the difference as an open question. A general commercial explanation is not a conclusion about an individual incident. Preserve written answers with their limiting language. Removing a qualification from a short summary can make the explanation appear broader than the actual wording supports.

Cyber risk needs separate assessment

An unavailable system alone does not establish malfunction, error or deliberate conduct. Record the observed effect and involve competent specialists. Do not publish logs, configurations, access details or suspected vulnerabilities to seek general opinions. This article provides no attack-detection, testing or investigation methods. Its purpose is to organize administrative questions without exposing systems or assigning an unsupported cause.

Distinguish physical property, digital services, third-party demands and response expenses in the insurance file. A description of material damage does not settle every cyber incident. Conversely, a cyber label alone does not establish acceptance of a particular cause or consequence. Read the documents according to their actual purpose instead of treating different categories as automatic substitutes.

Document an incident without exposing people

After safety measures and competent instructions, the administrative file can record communication chronology and documents already available. Do not ask staff to investigate unsafe places or objects for photographs. Do not alter or manipulate possible evidence on the basis of this article. Relevant professionals determine preservation and examination. Commercial documentation never takes priority over appropriate safety measures.

Separate confirmed information, hypotheses and another person's report. Identify source and date for each. An initial account can be incomplete without being false. If conclusions change after a competent report, retain versions and the explanation. Do not rewrite history as though every fact had been known initially. The documented update should show why the understanding changed.

Property values need an explainable basis

Prepare inventory, purchase records and relevant valuations with period and currency. Do not assume accounting value equals the amount needed for reinstatement. Ask about the basis required by the proposed contract. Identify company-owned assets, tenants' property and items managed for customers without duplication. Physical presence at one location does not make every item part of one insured interest.

For later costs, distinguish proposed measures, completed work and payments. Do not add several alternative repair quotations as if all were definitive losses. An internal estimate can assist planning without establishing insurer acceptance or legal allocation of the cost to someone. Preserve its assumptions and supporting documents so an estimate remains distinguishable from a final invoice or a third-party demand.

Continuity involves more than restarting machinery

Activity may need specialist checks, restored resources and reorganized orders before returning. Describe those stages generally for economic analysis and retain the assumptions. Do not publish security plans or operational procedures. Timing should be supported by competent staff, not invented or copied from another enterprise's scenario. A repaired component does not itself establish full operational recovery.

Separate continuing expenses, additional costs and delayed revenue. For interruption questions under a policy, request the relevant calculation basis and period. Total sales are not automatically lost profit. Operational continuity, accounting and contractual conditions need connections, but should not be treated as one process. An invoice dated during a shutdown also does not explain its cause merely through its date.

The role of official preparedness sources

IGSU publishes risk-preparedness information and guidance concerning the first 72 hours. Use official material for its proper purpose, not as evidence that an event is insured. This article reproduces no intervention protocol and does not decide actions for a particular dangerous situation. It provides no alternative to the competent instructions applicable to an actual threat.

Administratively, a company can check communication responsibilities and legitimate access to documents privately. There is no need to disclose those details publicly. Preparedness information, security assessment and policy review serve different functions. None justifies promising that an incident is impossible or that every loss will be recovered. A working record can support clarity without making either guarantee.

What to check before a commercial conclusion

Request the subject, definitions, entities, property and period of the proposed document. Read limits, excess, exclusions and notification. The excess is the insured's share of a loss under the contract. Ask about causes and consequences relevant to the company. Merely mentioning an item in a conversation does not establish acceptance. Availability and eligibility require individual confirmation.

Present the true chronology of known circumstances. A new contract does not establish acceptance of costs from a situation that has already arisen. Insurance ING Broker SRL is an insurance broker, not the authority classifying incidents or the insurer deciding payment. This article is not a terrorism or sabotage coverage offer and cannot confirm a response to an individual case.

An example of neutral wording

Imagine a business discovering that equipment cannot be used after damage. Its first summary identifies the asset, observation time and available records without assigning an author or intention. Competent specialists and authorities can examine facts within their roles. The team keeps its economic questions separate from classification, instead of selecting a cause simply to provide a quick explanation to management.

This hypothetical example describes neither a real incident nor how damage could be caused. Any insurance discussion should connect the contractual documents with relevant findings. Neutral wording is useful until verification; it confirms no product, guilt or payment. It preserves questions rather than disguising uncertainty as a confident legal or commercial conclusion.

Keep uncertainty visible in internal communication

Different teams can receive partial information during a difficult situation. Assigning responsibility for the administrative document version can reduce contradictions without replacing authorities. Messages should distinguish confirmed, reported and still-reviewed information. A document coordinator helps maintain that distinction, but does not acquire authority to determine technical cause, legal classification or an insurer's financial decision.

Retain what is necessary without wide distribution of sensitive images or records. Staff communication, an authority's request and a contractual notification may have different recipients and purposes. This article sets no mandatory procedure. It recommends avoiding document confusion and nonexistent conclusions. When information changes, preserve the source relationship rather than silently circulating a new version as though nothing had changed.

Read customer obligations in the actual contracts

A business can have delivery or service obligations while the cause of a stoppage remains under review. Prepare relevant agreements and communications without automatically declaring release from all duties or entitlement to payment. Competent legal advice is needed for the effect of provisions in the particular circumstances. An insurance discussion cannot independently decide those separate commercial relationships.

Separate penalties demanded by others, actual expenses and estimated losses. Do not treat them as included by the same insurance phrase. Distinct categories allow precise questions and show unconfirmed elements. They prevent a risk scenario becoming a commercial promise or legal interpretation. A demand is not automatically an established liability or an amount accepted by an insurer.

Frequently asked questions about sabotage and terrorism

Are they identical to vandalism in every policy?

Do not assume equivalence. Legal and contractual definitions need separate competent checking. An informal label or news report does not determine treatment of a particular situation.

Must I send security plans?

Not through a public form or for a general explanation. Begin with activities, property categories and available documents. Necessary sensitive information uses controlled channels and appropriate recipients.

Does property insurance cover every interruption?

Do not infer that. Check the actual event, assets, financial consequences and conditions. A short commercial description does not establish inclusion of every cause and expense.

Can this article be used as an intervention procedure?

No. Actual danger requires safety and competent authorities' instructions first. The article concerns administrative records and insurance questions, not investigation, security operations or technical manoeuvres.
